records.name: Cross River
records.summary: No state-specific trans-related source was found for this division in the current research pass: no local incident series and no documented enforcement divergence from the national frame. The national law applies here in full — the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 (up to 14 years, extends to tourists, bans LGBTQ+ organisations and public expression of identity) plus the inherited criminal provisions; national monitoring recorded 89 extortions, 118 harassment incidents and more than 20 unlawful detentions of LGBTQ+ people by law-enforcement officials in 2024 alone, with detentions for "looking gay" and release on payment of a bribe reported. This division sits outside the twelve northern states that carry a separate religious-law death-penalty regime for same-sex conduct. Dating-app "kito" extortion gangs are a nationwide app-user risk, and foreign government travel advice warns LGBT travellers of arrest, violence and blackmail.

records.name: Oyo
records.summary:
No regional protective statute, recorded incident series or documented enforcement divergence from the national framework has been documented for this state. The national framework applies in full: a 2014 statute punishes same-sex unions with up to 14 years' imprisonment and — as reported in August 2026 summarising a foreign government's travel advisory — also reaches assisting, attending or promoting same-sex ceremonies and LGBT+ organisations; religious criminal law in some northern states can carry the death penalty for same-sex conduct. The same advisory warns LGBT+ travellers to this country of arrest, violence, blackmail and intimidation.

The recorded violence pattern is national and recent: a 33-year-old transgender media personality and sex worker was beaten to death in the federal capital in August 2024, having reported a stabbing a year earlier and said she feared for her life; authorities ordered a discreet investigation. Mass arrests and detention of LGBT+ people remain common, concentrated in some northern states. The absence of state-specific records here reflects thin documentation rather than demonstrated safety.
